sections.heading: About this policy
sections.text: As It Is is a free app for reading the books of His Divine Grace A. C. Bhaktivedanta Swami Prabhupāda. This policy says what the app does with information about you. Questions are welcome at support@asitis.cc.

sections.heading: Your name and mobile number
sections.text: When you first open the app, it asks for your name and mobile number. They are saved on your phone and sent to the app's registration database (Google Firebase Cloud Firestore), together with the app's version and the platform (Android), under an anonymous Firebase sign-in that the app creates on your phone. No password, email address, location or contacts are asked for.

sections.heading: Why they are asked for
sections.text: Only to identify the app's readers, for our internal records, and to count them.

sections.heading: Who sees them
sections.text: Your name and mobile number are not sold and are not shared with anyone. They are kept in the app's own Firebase project; Google runs Firebase as the service that stores them.

sections.heading: Your reading
sections.text: Highlights, notes, bookmarks, reading progress and settings stay on your phone. The app does not send them anywhere, and Android's backup is turned off for the app.

sections.heading: When the app uses the internet
sections.text: The books are read offline. The app goes online only to: send your registration (above); on its first start, show the app's key server (keys.asitis.cc) that the phone has not been changed, and receive the key that opens the books (the phone's own security chip signs a certificate naming the app and the phone's security state, such as whether its bootloader is locked: no name, number or other personal detail); download the books' library once, from the app's server on Cloudflare or, if that does not answer, the app's GitHub repository; check for a new version, and read the text that Share app shares and the app's messages, from the same two places; and download Google's English–Hindi language pack, once, if you agree to it. Translation itself then happens on your phone. Google Define and Google Translate open Google in your browser with the words you selected; Google's own privacy policy applies there. Like any website, Cloudflare, GitHub and Google receive the usual connection details, such as your internet address, when the app or your browser contacts them.

sections.heading: Crash details
sections.text: If the app closes because of an error, the details (the app's and Android's version, the phone model, the time and the error) are kept on your phone. They are sent only if you choose Send details, by your own email app, to support@asitis.cc. Nothing you wrote or read is in them.

sections.heading: Removing your details
sections.text: To have your name and mobile number removed from the registration database, write to support@asitis.cc. Uninstalling the app removes everything it kept on your phone.

sections.heading: Changes
sections.text: If this policy changes, the new version is published at this same address, with its date above.
